concrete_examples.description: In NetHack, items such as potions and scrolls are initially identified as 'unknown' when picked up, requiring players to use them to discover their effects. This adds a layer of risk, as a potion could be beneficial or harmful, prompting players to weigh the potential consequences before using an unidentified item.

In broguece, unidentified items are represented with a question mark, and players must use a specific resource, such as identification scrolls or a skill, to reveal their properties. This mechanic introduces a strategic layer as players must decide when to use limited resources to identify items, weighing the potential benefits against the risks of using unknown items.

In 'Crawl', players encounter unidentified items that can include weapons, armor, and potions. To learn their properties, players must either use them (which carries the risk of negative effects) or use a limited resource like scrolls of identify, creating strategic decisions around resource management and risk assessment.

In cataclysm-bn, items are initially unidentified and players must use resources like identification scrolls or spend time to reveal their properties. This creates a risk-reward scenario where players must decide whether to use an unknown item, potentially facing negative effects.

definition: A game mechanic where items must be identified before their properties are known. This creates information asymmetry and risk — using an unknown item may be beneficial or harmful. Identification consumes resources or creates gameplay decisions.
exclusion_criteria: Identification that is free and instantaneous
Items that are purely cosmetic without hidden properties
inclusion_criteria: Items have unknown properties until identified
Identification requires resources, spells, or actions
Identification creates strategic decisions (identify now vs later)
title: Item Identification System
